items.title: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
items.summary: The models responsible for last month’s agent hack of Hugging Face had been inadvertently trained to cheat and to communicate with each other, according to an OpenAI technical report released today. The hack, which a group of agents undertook to find solutions for a cybersecurity test that they were stuck on, has confirmed some experts’…

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, targeting "ultimate cost efficiency"
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team is previewing the Qwen4 architecture with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a mixture-of-experts model that activates just 6 out of 125 billion parameters per token. At one-ninth the training cost, it beats much larger competitors like DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Claude Opus 4.6 on coding and office benchmarks, adding more pricing pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic....

items.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
items.summary: OpenAI shares findings from the Hugging Face security incident and the steps we’re taking to strengthen AI model security, monitoring, and alignment.

items.title: Surprise: Z.ai is the AI lab behind the mysterious Ox Alpha model
items.summary: Z.ai confirms it is behind Ox Alpha, the mysterious open AI model topping benchmarks and leaderboards, and its weights are set to be released soon.

items.title: Chinese Moonshot AI negotiates hosting deals with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google
items.summary: A Chinese AI company could land its model on major US cloud platforms for the first time, taking a cut of the revenue. The article Chinese Moonshot AI negotiates hosting deals with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: OpenAI releases its official report on the Hugging Face breach
items.summary: The report, which spans several discrete cybersecurity compromises, is the most complete accounting of the incident to date.

items.title: Jalapeño’s first results show industry-leading speed and efficiency in AI inference
items.summary: Jalapeño is a custom inference chip from OpenAI that delivers faster, more power-efficient AI inference, with higher throughput and lower latency for modern models.

items.title: Presentation: Can Claude Fix Itself? Using LLMs for Incident Response
items.summary: Anthropic reliability engineer Alex Palcuie shares practical lessons on using LLMs for real-world incident response. He explains where AI acts as a superhuman for observing logs and traces, why it still struggles with causation versus correlation during root-cause analysis, and how engineering leaders can integrate AI into on-call workflows without eroding human expertise. By Alex Palcuie

items.title: QueryStory wants you to believe what AI is telling you
items.summary: The startup came out of stealth with $6 million in seed funding and a plan to use LLMs and cybersecurity know-how to make AI queries coherent.

items.title: The full stack behind abundant intelligence
items.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar explains how advances across chips, compute, models, and products compound to deliver more useful intelligence at greater scale and lower cost.

items.title: IBM drops open-weight Granite 4.2 family with built-in agentic capabilities under Apache 2.0
items.summary: IBM is releasing its Granite 4.2 language models in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes, trained on about 15 trillion tokens with a context window of up to 512,000 tokens. The larger models use "agentic RL" training to learn tool use and code execution on their own. All models are available under the Apache 2.0 license....
